mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer discretionary spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1400K units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, increasing borrowing costs and predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 3.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the tight labor market fuels wage inflation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased consumer spending.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market influence on inflation
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both trigger conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month, indicating supply chain resilience, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeding 2.5% on a quarterly basis signals strong economic demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP influence on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth surpasses 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 6-month moving average predicts the direction of S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, with higher rates relative to average indicating negative returns.
failure_condition: Mechanism's predictive power (Rank IC) falls below 0.01 over a 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) and high payroll employment growth (PAYEMS > 150K in a month) amplifies the positive effect on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as a tight labor market boosts economic growth.
evidence_refs: fact:combined labor market indicators' influence on growth
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly higher in triggered instances compared to non-triggered (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Regime-conditional: during post-shock recovery, a rebound in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1.5% in a month predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as consumer spending drives the recovery.
failure_condition: Mechanism fails to predict positive SPX returns in > 55% of post-shock recovery instances when RSAFS growth exceeds 1.5%.
